newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA UNLIKELY TO UNDERESTIMATE FAROES IN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA UNLIKELY TO UNDERESTIMATE FAROES IN WORLD CUP.

text.p: Yugoslav coach Slobodan Santrac said on Monday his team would not under-estimate minnows Faroe Islands when he named his squad for Saturday's group six world cup qualifying match.
Yugoslavia, who only have four home-based players in the squad, only narrowly beat the Faroes 3-2 at home in April.
"Despite the fact that the Faroes are not among the strongest opponents, we are taking the upcoming game very seriously," Santrac said on television.
"A defeat against an outsider cannot be made up in another game since everyone is counting on points in games against Malta and the Faroes," Santrac said.

All of the squad have arrived in Belgrade except for Savo Milosevic who will arrive on Tuesday following Aston Villa's match against Newcastle in the English league on Monday night. The squad will leave for the Faroes on Thursday.
Goalkeepers: Zoran Kocic (Perugia), Zvonko Milojevic (Red Star Belgrade)

Defenders: Risto Vidakovic, (Real Betis, Spain), Goran Djorovic (Red Star Belgrade), Miroslav Djukic (Deportivo La Coruna, Spain), Dejan Stefanovic (Sheffield Wednesday, England), Nisa Saveljic (Partizan Belgrade), Bratislav Zivkovic (Red Star Belgrade) Midfield: Branko Brnovic (Espanyol, Spain), Slavisa Jokanovic (Tenerife, Spain), Vladimir Jugovic (Juventus, Italy), Sinisa Mihajlovic (Sampdoria, Italy), Dragan Stojkovic (Nagoya, Japan), Dejan Savicevic (Milan, Italy), Albert Nadj (Real Betis), Dejan Govedarica (Volendam, Netherlands) Forwards: Predrag Mijatovic (Real Madrid, Spain), Savo Milosevic (Aston Villa, England), Darko Kovacevic (Real Sociedad), Anto Drobnjak (Bastia, France)
